evidence.text: Capri has guided low and printed above its own quarterly bar on the last two prints. Q1 FY27 adj EPS was $0.67 against $0.39 consensus, revenue $769M against $757M; Q4 FY26 was $0.22 against $0.12. The Q2 guide of $780M / $0.20, which consensus ($786.6M / $0.21) now matches, embeds two items that are timing rather than demand: ~$50M of Michael Kors inventory held up by Asian port congestion, and ~$10M of wholesale shipments pulled into Q1. The likely Q2 print is therefore modestly above the bar (I put revenue about +1%).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name has sold beats. Q1 FY27 (2026-08-05) beat EPS by 72% with a revenue beat but cut the FY revenue guide, and the stock fell 3.03%. Q4 FY26 (2026-05-27) beat EPS and fell 1.24%. Q3 FY26 (2026-02-03) fell 13.22%. The only large up move was +14.51% on 2025-08-06.
evidence.why_not_priced: If the habitual beat were priced, consensus would sit above the guide (it sits at $0.21 against $0.20 and $786.6M against $780M) and the stock would have run into the print. Instead it is -4.25% over 5 days, with the skew paying for downside. What is not priced is how big the beat is. The reaction function caps the size of this finding.
evidence.independence: Q2 guide composition (the $50M inventory delay and the $10M wholesale timing shift) is from the company release: https://www.capriholdings.com/news/news-details/2026/Capri-Holdings-Limited-Announces-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027-Results/default.aspx. The same document family as the bar, so this is one finding, not two.

evidence.text: The Asian port congestion that Capri blamed for ~$50M of lost Q2 Michael Kors revenue (called 'temporary' on Aug 5) had not cleared by October. Dimerco's October 2026 Asia-Pac freight report (published ~Oct 1) says Shanghai would stay heavily congested into mid-to-late October with berthing waits above 5 days, Yantian was under intake limits, and Asia-US ocean rates were rising on blank sailings to near-pandemic levels, pushing cargo to air. That puts Q3 holiday inventory flow and freight cost at risk, and with them the H2 Michael Kors return to growth that the FY $3.4B guide rests on.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Aug 5 2026 FY revenue cut (from $3.525B to $3.4B, partly on these same inventory delays) drew -3.03% despite a large EPS beat. In Feb 2026 a guidance/trend disappointment drew -13.22%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus FY revenue still sits at about the $3.4B guide, and the Q2 guide treated the congestion as a one-quarter timing item. If the market expected it to persist into Q3, FY estimates would be below guide, which no source shows. The 6-vol-point put skew may partly carry it.
evidence.independence: Proxy: freight-forwarder data, not a Capri statement on Q3. The company's own attribution to Asian port congestion is in https://english.aawsat.com/fashion/5303799-capri-cuts-revenue-outlook-iran-war-hits-michael-kors-sales (2026-08-05). The same Dimerco content is covered by https://www.sdcexec.com/transportation/trucking/news/22975771/dimerco-peak-season-extended-asia-freight-demand-exceeds-forecasts (one underlying report).

evidence.text: Short interest nearly doubled into the print: 7.9M shares on 2026-07-31, 14.3M on 2026-10-15 (~12.6% of shares outstanding, 4.48 days to cover). On top of that, WWD reported in late September that Capri has informally approached potential acquirers. That combination puts a squeeze and takeover-optionality floor under any print that does not cut the FY guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior print with this short build. The +14.51% move on 2025-08-06 is the name's one large upside reaction, and it came off a depressed base.
evidence.why_not_priced: Positioning is not a fact the market misses. It is the asymmetry: shorts at 4.5 days to cover pay more on a relief print than longs lose on a disappointment. The call-heavy open interest (put/call 0.45) agrees with this; the put skew does not.
evidence.independence: Sale exploration: https://fashionunited.com/news/business/is-capri-holdings-up-for-sale/2026092574852 (late Sept 2026, citing WWD; informal, a near-term deal unlikely).

evidence.text: Peers that reported after Capri's Aug 5 guide show European and Middle East demand weaker in Jul-Sep. Moncler's Q3 EMEA was -8% on weaker domestic demand and fewer tourists. Hermès grew in every region except the Middle East. LVMH's CFO called the Middle East still a headwind. Capri guided only ~$15M of softer EMEA in Q2 ($50M for the FY). Michael Kors EMEA was $142M in Q1 (-5.3%) and Jimmy Choo EMEA $82M, so a further low-single-digit EMEA shortfall is ~$5-10M.
evidence.source_date: 2026-10 (Moncler Q3 to 30 Sept 2026; exact publication day not shown)
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: EMEA softness was one of three reasons for the Aug 5 FY revenue cut (-3.03% reaction). No separate history on this line.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus revenue sits at or slightly above the guide ($786.6M against $780M). If the peer EMEA weakness had been pushed through, estimates would sit below the guide.
evidence.independence: Hermès Q3 2026: every region grew except the Middle East, https://www.pursebop.com/hermes-holds-the-reins-in-q3-2026-as-leather-goods-lead/. Peer proxy only; Capri has not commented since Aug 5.

evidence.text: US luxury demand held up in Jul-Sep at the peers that have reported. Prada's Americas grew +5% organic in Q3 (the strongest region). Kering said North America was Gucci's most resilient market, with Kering NA up 2%. LVMH said the US was still growing. Michael Kors Americas is ~63% of MK revenue ($372M in Q1, -9.9%), so this is a modest support for the Q2 Americas line. Net of the rest: the Q1 Americas decline was brand-specific (fewer promotions, less off-price), so peer strength transmits only weakly.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: MK Americas fell 9.9% in Q1 FY27 and the stock fell 3.03%. No print in the baseline shows a positive reaction to an Americas beat.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. It is high-end luxury read across to an accessible-luxury brand, which is why the size is small. Tapestry, the closest US comparable, does not report until Nov 5, so the market has no direct US accessible-luxury read yet.
evidence.independence: Kering Q3 2026, NA most resilient for Gucci: https://fashionunited.uk/news/business/kering-q3-revenue-remains-stable-as-jewelry-and-eyewear-offset-gucci-contraction/2026102391016 (2026-10-23). LVMH Q3: https://fashionunited.com/news/business/lvmh-q3-organic-revenue-growth-slows-amid-china-downturn/2026101375147 (2026-10-13).

evidence.text: The euro weakened after Capri set its 'updated foreign currency exchange rate assumptions' on Aug 5. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: FX was one of the reasons for the Aug 5 FY revenue cut (-3.03%).
evidence.why_not_priced: FX is public and estimates usually absorb it, so most of this is priced. What remains is whether Capri trims the FY revenue line again for it on the call.

evidence.text: Management's own comp math favours holding the FY guide. H1 comp was -2.9% (Q1 -3.7%, Q2 -2.1%), so the -2% midpoint needs H2 at about -1.1%. evidence.text: REAL beat the top of its own guide on every line last quarter: Q2 GMV $617M against a $590-600M guide (+2.8% over the top), revenue $192.6M against $186-189M (+1.9% over the top), adj EBITDA $13.5M against $11-12M. Its Q3 guide (GMV $610-620M, revenue $194-198M) implies GMV +17-19% YoY against Q3 2025's $520M, after +22% in Q2 and +24% in Q1. It also implies sequential GMV of -1% to +0.5%, against +3% Q2-to-Q3 in 2025. The same 2-3% beat would put Q3 at roughly $630-635M GMV and $200-201M revenue, about 2% over the ~$197M street bar.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats above the top of the guide were sold three times in 2026: Q1 beat (GMV +24%, guide raised) -17.26%; Q2 beat and raise -3.68%; Q4 2025 -1.05%. They were bought in 2025: Q3 2025 +38.09%, Q2 2025 +16.15% (baseline history).
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The street's ~$197M sits near the top of the guide rather than above it, so a repeat 2-3% beat is not fully in consensus. But the stock has run +29% in 20 days and implied vol is 101%, so the buy side may already hold a whisper above consensus. If the beat were fully priced, consensus would sit above the guide top ($198M+), as it does for Q4.
evidence.independence: Q2 guide figures are from the Q1 coverage (https://fashionunited.uk/news/business/the-realreal-achieves-double-digit-growth-in-q1-2026/2026050887931); Q3 2025 base from the 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1573221/000157322125000076/real-20251110xex991pressre.htm). Same company documents throughout; the eBay and LVMH findings are the independent read on demand.

evidence.text: REAL raised the FY far more than the size of its beat. After Q2 the FY revenue guide went from $770-784M to $788-797M (+$15.5M at the midpoint) on a ~$5M beat of the Q2 guide midpoint. The street Q4 revenue consensus of $216.5M (UBS expects a Q4 guide of $214-218M) sits at the top of what the current FY guide implies for Q4 ($211-216M if Q3 lands at the $196M midpoint). An in-line FY reiteration would therefore disappoint, and the bar is a raise, which the company has delivered at both 2026 prints.
evidence.source_date: 2026-10-22 (UBS action date per https://www.investing.com/equities/therealreal-inc-consensus-estimates; the article itself is undated)
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Both 2026 FY raises were followed by declines (-17.26% after Q1, -3.68% after Q2). The Q3 2025 FY raise was followed by +38.09%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The Q4 consensus already assumes a raise, so only a raise above ~$218M is new. Sized small because the Q4 bar has one relay source and the stock sold both 2026 raises.
evidence.independence: The FY guide history is in the company releases (https://finviz.com/news/378972/the-realreal-announces-second-quarter-2026-results). The Q4 consensus rests only on the UBS/Finimize relay.

evidence.text: eBay reported on 2026-10-28, the day before REAL, Q3 2026 GMV of $23.2B (+15% reported, +16% FX-neutral). US GMV was $12.5B, +27% YoY, against international +4%. eBay cited recommerce leadership, an expanded luxury Authenticity Guarantee and the closed Depop acquisition (2.5 points of total growth). Its October Recommerce Report has 47% of consumers buying secondhand at least monthly, against 35% in 2025.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No REAL reaction is on record for an eBay print. REAL rose about 4% intraday on 2026-10-29, the session after eBay's release (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/545822-why-the-realreal-inc8217s-real-stock-is-down-621).
evidence.why_not_priced: It came out the day before the print and is a proxy. Depop and C2C collectibles inflate eBay's US number, so the read-through to authenticated consigned luxury is loose. The +4% intraday move on 10-29 may already hold some of it.
evidence.independence: Proxy, not company-confirmed. Points the same way as LVMH's statement that the US grew in Q3 (https://www.lvmh.com/en/publications/continued-growth-in-the-third-quarter-of-2026).

evidence.text: LVMH's Q3 2026 release (2026-10-12) says the US, Europe and Japan all grew. Group organic growth was ~+1%, and Fashion & Leather Goods fell 5% organically on China. US luxury demand held up while new-luxury pricing and volume were soft, which supports both the resale buyer and consignor supply that REAL's CEO credited for the Q2 raise.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured REAL reaction to LVMH prints.
evidence.why_not_priced: Public for 17 days, a macro proxy, and two-sided: weak new luxury can mean cheaper resale supply or a softer luxury consumer. Small.
evidence.independence: https://fashionunited.com/news/business/lvmh-q3-organic-revenue-growth-slows-amid-china-downturn/2026101375147 reports the same data. Points the same way as the eBay US figure.

evidence.text: REAL marks its warrant liability ($74.7M at 2026-06-30) to its share price, and Q2 took an $18.6M non-cash loss on it as the stock rose. The stock fell from about $11.79 on 2026-06-30 to about $8.95 around 2026-10-01 (implied by the baseline's +28.9% 20-day run-up to $11.54). Q3 should therefore carry a non-cash warrant gain of the order of $15M+, which could make GAAP net income and EPS print far better than the $(0.23) of Q2 and better than an algo-read consensus.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 carried a -$44M warrant loss and the stock rose +38.09%; Q2 2026 carried -$18.6M and fell -3.68%. The line has not driven the reaction.
evidence.why_not_priced: Below operating income, non-cash, and the street trades on adj EBITDA. It only matters for headline-GAAP-reading algos in the first minutes. [sizing note removed].
evidence.independence: June 30 close $11.79 from https://eulerpool.com/stock/US88339P1012; the end-of-quarter level comes from the sealed baseline.

evidence.text: On 2026-10-15 REAL refinanced its 13.00% all-in (8.75% cash + 4.25% PIK) 2029 senior secured notes with a $150M Fortress term loan at SOFR+5.75%, all cash, plus an undrawn $25M revolver. Both mature in October 2033. The company expects about $4M less interest expense in year one and set a medium-term target to cut total leverage to $150M, alongside a 15-20% adj EBITDA margin target. The money buys a cheaper, longer maturity on existing debt; no distress signal was found.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock rose about 11.5% on the 2026-10-15 announcement (https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-2166948-20261016).
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced on the day. The only open part is the call's detail on the path to $150M leverage (the 2028 converts, conversion of the 2031s). That could read as deleveraging or as dilution.
evidence.independence: 8-K body https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001573221/000119312526422329/d170302d8k.htm is the same document family.

evidence.text: Positioning into the print is stretched long. The stock is up +28.9% in 20 days and +10.1% in 5 days to $11.54. Open interest is almost all calls (put/call 0.03), and the skew still pays for downside (+5.25 vol points). UBS cut its target to $14 from $16 on 2026-10-22, calling a solid quarter 'basically what analysts already expect' and cutting on valuation. Short interest also rose to 17.5M shares (14.4% of shares outstanding, 5.8 days to cover), from 14.8M in mid-August. Each 2026 beat-and-raise has been sold.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026 prints: -1.05%, -17.26%, -3.68%, all sold despite beats. The last print with a large run-up and a beat (Q1 2026) fell -17.26%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The run-up and skew are themselves the market's statement. What is new is the combination of a valuation cut by an analyst and a reaction function that has sold three beats. Shrunk because the 14.4% short and 5.8 days to cover are a squeeze mechanism on a clean beat.
evidence.independence: UBS cut: https://www.investing.com/equities/therealreal-inc-consensus-estimates (2026-10-22). Run-up and skew come from the sealed baseline.

evidence.text: Revenue keeps growing about 5 points slower than GMV: Q2 revenue +17% against GMV +22%, take rate 35.9%, down ~200bp YoY on a mix shift to higher-value items. The Q3 guide implies revenue/GMV of ~31.9% (at midpoints $196M/$615M) against 33.5% in Q3 2025 ($174M/$520M). That is no normalisation, although the Q1 call said take-rate pressure would ease in H2. A further take-rate decline is the 'quality of beat' line a bear can trade on.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 (take rate -220bp) fell -17.26% despite a revenue beat and raise; the cause is not established in any source found.
evidence.why_not_priced: It sits inside what the company guided, so the market was told to expect it. It is small unless take rate prints below ~35% or the call stops promising H2 normalisation.
evidence.independence: Q2 take rate from the company release (https://finviz.com/news/378972/the-realreal-announces-second-quarter-2026-results); Q3 2025 base from the 8-K. Shares documents with the first finding but reads a different line (take rate rather than volume).
